q: The standard of length is _____.
e: The standard of length is metre. The physics in this sentence is built around metre involving length.

q: The metre was originally defined as the length between two marks on a platinum-iridium rod at _____, kept at the International Bureau of Weights and Measures at Sevres, near Paris.
e: The metre was originally defined as the length between two marks on a platinum-iridium rod at $0^{\circ}\text{C}$, kept at the International Bureau of Weights and Measures at Sevres, near Paris. By definition that quantity is $0^{\circ}\text{C}$.

q: Nowadays the standard of length used is based on the wavelength of orange-red light emitted by a _____ isotope.
e: Nowadays the standard of length used is based on the wavelength of orange-red light emitted by a krypton 86 isotope. Wavelength is crest to next crest, and v equals f lambda involving used.

q: A metre is now defined as the length equivalent to _____ times the wavelength of orange-red light emitted by a krypton 86 isotope.
e: A metre is now defined as the length equivalent to $1\,650\,763.73$ times the wavelength of orange-red light emitted by a krypton 86 isotope. Wavelength is crest to next crest, and v equals f lambda.

q: In 1983, the metre was given a new operational definition based on the speed of _____.
e: In 1983, the metre was given a new operational definition based on the speed of light. The physics in this sentence is built around light.

q: The metre is the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of _____ of a second.
e: The metre is the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of $1/299\,792\,458$ of a second. The physics in this sentence is built around $1/299\,792\,458$.

q: In the CGS system the unit of length is the centimetre (cm) and $1 ext{ cm} = $ _____.
e: In the CGS system the unit of length is the centimetre (cm) and $1 ext{ cm} = $ $10^{-2}\text{ m}$. The physics in this sentence is built around $10^{-2}\text{ m}$.

q: In the FPS system the unit of length is the foot (ft) and $1 ext{ ft} = $ _____.
e: In the FPS system the unit of length is the foot (ft) and $1 ext{ ft} = $ $0.3048\text{ m}$. The physics in this sentence is built around $0.3048\text{ m}$.

q: The unit of length used by particle physicists is the 'Fermi' or 'femtometre' (fm) given by $1 ext{ fm} = $ _____.
e: The unit of length used by particle physicists is the 'Fermi' or 'femtometre' (fm) given by $1 ext{ fm} = $ $10^{-15}\text{ m}$. The physics in this sentence is built around $10^{-15}\text{ m}$.

q: In the field of optics, physicists use the unit angstrom ($ ext{\AA}$), where $1 ext{ \AA} = $ _____.
e: In the field of optics, physicists use the unit angstrom ($ ext{\AA}$), where $1 ext{ \AA} = $ $10^{-10}\text{ m}$. The physics in this sentence is built around $10^{-10}\text{ m}$.

q: In astronomy, the most suitable units are the astronomical unit (AU) and the _____ unit (ly).
e: In astronomy, the most suitable units are the astronomical unit (AU) and the light year unit (ly). The physics in this sentence is built around light year.

q: The light year is the distance which light travels in _____.
e: The light year is the distance which light travels in one year. The physics in this sentence is built around one year involving which.

q: The value of $1 ext{ AU}$ is equal to _____.
e: The value of $1 ext{ AU}$ is equal to $9.461 \times 10^{15}\text{ m}$. The physics in this sentence is built around $9.461 \times 10^{15}\text{ m}$.

q: The value of $1 ext{ ly}$ is equal to _____.
e: The value of $1 ext{ ly}$ is equal to $1.496 \times 10^{11}\text{ m}$. The physics in this sentence is built around $1.496 \times 10^{11}\text{ m}$.

q: The largest unit of length is the _____.
e: The largest unit of length is the parsec. The unit that belongs with this quantity is parsec.

q: The value of $1 ext{ pc}$ is equal to _____.
e: The value of $1 ext{ pc}$ is equal to $3.084 \times 10^{16}\text{ m}$. The physics in this sentence is built around $3.084 \times 10^{16}\text{ m}$.

q: The standard of mass is a cylinder of $1 ext{ kg}$ mass made of _____ alloy.
e: The standard of mass is a cylinder of $1 ext{ kg}$ mass made of platinum-iridium alloy. The physics in this sentence is built around platinum-iridium.

q: The standard kilogram is kept at the International Bureau of Weights and Measures at _____, near Paris.
e: The standard kilogram is kept at the International Bureau of Weights and Measures at Lyon, near Paris. The physics in this sentence is built around Lyon.

q: The SI base unit of time is the _____.
e: The SI base unit of time is the hour. SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit.

q: The second was originally defined as $1/(60 imes 60 imes 24)$ of a _____.
e: The second was originally defined as $1/(60 imes 60 imes 24)$ of a day. By definition that quantity is day.

q: For accuracy, the second is now defined in terms of the frequency of oscillation which can occur from a _____ atom.
e: For accuracy, the second is now defined in terms of the frequency of oscillation which can occur from a krypton atom. Frequency counts complete waves per second, and v equals f lambda.

q: A particular frequency of _____ $ ext{s}^{-1}$ emitted or absorbed by a cesium atom is used to define $1 ext{ s}$.
e: A particular frequency of $9\,192\,631\,770$ $ ext{s}^{-1}$ emitted or absorbed by a cesium atom is used to define $1 ext{ s}$. Frequency counts complete waves per second, and v equals f lambda.
